title: Heartbreaking News Revealed Following The Death Of 30-Year-Old Ex-NFLer - NewsBreak
text:
By Alex Hoegler ,
1 hours ago
Police tape (Photo via Imagn Images) More heartbreaking news has surfaced following the death of former NFL cornerback Chris Payton-Jones.
Tragically, Chris Payton-Jones died in a car accident in Gainesville, Florida, at the age of 30 on Saturday. The former Nebraska star played 29 games over four NFL seasons and had a brief stint with the St. Louis Battlehawks of the United Football League.
Making his untimely death even more crushing? His sister, Clotea Jones, told The Sun that Payton-Jones had just become a father three weeks earlier:
“He was excited about where he was in life, working with kids and the birth of his daughter,” Jones told the outlet. “His daughter was born 3 weeks before he passed. He was just excited about being a father.”
According to The Sun , Chris Payton-Jones was driving in the wrong lane when his vehicle collided with a pickup truck. The driver and two passengers suffered minor injuries.
Our thoughts and prayers are with Payton-Jones’ family and friends during this difficult time.
Chris Payton-Jones Began His Pro Career With Arizona Cardinals Chris Payton-Jones breaking up a pass in XFL game (Credit: Steven Bisig-USA TODAY Sports) The Jacksonville native initially signed as an undrafted free agent with the Detroit Lions in 2018. After getting waived, he was picked up by the Arizona Cardinals, then coached by Steve Wilks.
Payton-Jones appeared in two games for the Cardinals as a rookie. He got more playing time as a sophomore in 2019 (Kyler Murray’s rookie year), logging six pass breakups and 22 combined tackles in 11 games.
During the 2020 season, Payton-Jones was added back to the Lions’ practice squad. He played one game before getting picked up off waivers from the Minnesota Vikings, where he’d play eight games.
Payton-Jones spent his final NFL season with the Tennessee Titans in 2021. He had one pass breakup in seven games.
